title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 2 of a 1986 note on 'disjonctions'. The heading reads 'Spatios', not 'Syntaxes'; see the corrections. Grothendieck announces 'two ways to describe' the notion.

Definition 1. A spatio is a set Σ with a relation ≤ and a map C satisfying:
- Spt 1: ≤ is a partial order with arbitrary Sup and Inf, i.e. a complete lattice, with bottom 0_Σ and top 1_Σ.
- Spt 2: C is an involution (C(Cx) = x) that reverses order: x ≤ y ⇔ Cy ≤ Cx.
- Spt 3: x ∧ Cx = 0_Σ for all x, equivalently x ∨ Cx = 1_Σ.

Corollaries of Spt 2: Cor 1 says C turns Sup into Inf and Inf into Sup (De Morgan). Cor 2 says C0 = 1 and C1 = 0.

In modern language, a spatio is exactly a complete ortholattice. It is neither assumed distributive (that would give a complete Boolean algebra) nor orthomodular.

A passage is crossed out here and rewritten on the next page. It equips a spatio with a canonical 'disjonction' (orthogonality) relation: x |0| y ⇔ x ≤ Cy, which is symmetric by Spt 2.

The previous page supplies the source of examples. A 'disjonction' on a set E is a symmetric relation, with a set E_0 of self-disjoint points. Σ_E is the family of subsets closed under the double-polar ('cos-W') operation. It is closed under arbitrary intersections, with C(A) = polar of A. By the next page, (Σ_E, ⊂, C) is a spatio, and there is a canonical map E → Σ_E.

This is the classical passage from an orthogonality space to the complete ortholattice of its biorthogonally closed subsets (Birkhoff polarities, MacLaren, Dacey, Foulis–Randall). The 'two ways to describe' are presumably the lattice-with-complement description and the disjonction-space description, related by the map E → Σ_E. The problem served is building 'spatial' objects from a discrete disjointness structure; the immediate goal is the Ateliers chapter's construction.
errors: No mathematical errors. Spt 3's two forms are correctly shown equivalent via Cor 1 and 2: apply C to x ∧ Cx = 0 to get Cx ∨ x = 1.
Cor 1 needs only that C is an order anti-automorphism, which follows from Spt 2. This is correct.

ideas.what: Spatio: a complete lattice with an order-reversing involution C such that x ∧ Cx = 0
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff–von Neumann (1936) for orthocomplemented lattices; Birkhoff, Lattice Theory (1940)

ideas.what: Canonical disjonction (orthogonality) on a spatio: x |0| y iff x ≤ Cy, symmetric and downward-closed
ideas.modern_name: orthogonality relation induced by an orthocomplementation

ideas.what: Duality between disjonction structures on sets and spatios, via closed subsets Σ_E and the canonical map E → Σ_E (continued on adjacent pages)
ideas.modern_name: orthogonality spaces and their ortholattices of biorthogonally closed sets (Galois-connection closure)

missed.claim: Grothendieck, apparently independently, rebuilds the orthogonality-space ↔ complete-ortholattice framework of quantum logic. He frames it as 'spatios' (space-like objects) built from discrete 'disjonction' structures. Neither the link to quantum logic / orthospaces nor this 'spatial' interpretation by Grothendieck is recorded. The mathematics itself is classical, though.
missed.quote: Une spatio est un ensemble Σ, muni d'une relation ≤, et d'une application C ... C est une involution (C(Cx)=x) et "renverse la relation d'ordre"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents Grothendieck's 1986 interest in discrete or combinatorial foundations of 'space'. It does not give new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the standard definition of a complete ortholattice and its induced orthogonality relation. It is interesting only as evidence of Grothendieck's 1986 reinvention of quantum-logic structures under the name 'spatio'.
transcription_corrections: Heading is '2. Spatios' (not 'Syntaxes'), and 'Une spatio est un ensemble Σ' (not 'Une syntaxe').
The parenthetical reads roughly 'd'une application C (relation aussi, mais oui !)'. Here C is an involutive map.

Crossed-out passage: 'À une spatio on associe une structure de disjonction canonique, en posant x |0| y ⇔ x ≤ Cy (⇔ y ≤ Cx par Spt 2)'. The symbol is |0| (disjonction), not ⊥, and the word is 'disjonction', not 'dispositions commutative'.
First line is likely 'Cela montre que pour ce construction...', continuing from the previous page.
